propositions: Four model-provenance guards each invoke _run_request_sites() independently, causing the same whole-tree AST analysis to be computed four times per test session instead of once

Within each _run_request_sites() call, _verdict's parameter-provenance branch re-walks the entire src/rebar tree and re-parses every file once per RunRequest site with a parameter-provenance config, causing thousands of redundant parses per single scan

The analysis is a pure function of committed src/rebar source code with no test-time mutations or external dependencies consulted during AST scanning, making it safe to cache across all four guards within a test session

Caching _run_request_sites via a session-scoped pytest fixture and memoizing per-path parse operations via functools.cache removes both layers of redundant computation while producing identical (key, expr, verdict) tuples in the same order

Single-scan performance improves from 11.83s to 4.14s (-65%) via parse memoization, and four-guard wall time improves from 46.45s to ~4.14s + ~0.08s (-91%) via session fixture, with no change to assertion bodies or guard coverage
